Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting to blueprint our private VPC deployment and need to lock down an admission-control approach and initial rightsizing for the GPU pool that will serve our customer-facing inference endpoints. High level:

- Expected steady-state: ~150 QPS of short-chat style requests (avg 60 tokens output, avg 120 tokens input).
- Peak spikes: up to 1,200 QPS sustained for short windows (1-10 minutes) during campaign-driven bursts.
- Latency target: 95th <= 220ms for L1 (critical interactive flows), fallback to smaller model for non-critical.
- Models: quantized 8-bit and 16-bit variants, KV-cache enabled.
- Network: VPC peering to our on-prem app gateways, bandwidth currently 10Gbps between app layer and GPU subnet.

Attached is a traffic profile export and a simple network topo. Questions we want help with:

1) Recommended admission-control policy (concurrency vs tokens-per-second vs rate-smoothing) to guarantee L1 latency while allowing absorbing bursts without overprovisioning.
2) How to translate our QPS / token distribution into conservative GPU counts (include warm-pool and headroom guidance).
3) Practical guardrails for ingress (token caps, request batching windows, eviction rules for KV cache) and how Redwood recommends implementing them in a private VPC.

Can we schedule a 60-min run-through? Prefer Wed or Thu this week.

Thanks,

Sophie — thanks for the clear profile and the topo. We're inline to help. High level approach and immediate suggestions below; attaching a short admission-policy stub you can drop into your staging cluster.

Top-level strategy (short):
- Admission control: enforce a hybrid policy — per-model concurrency caps + a global token-per-second (TPS) envelope. Concurrency caps protect per-GPU memory/KV cache; TPS envelope prevents token storms that blow latency.
- Warm pool / headroom: size a warm pool equal to ~10-15% of steady-state GPU count and maintain an additional 20-30% transient headroom for bursts (with fast spin-up drivers).
- Fallbacks: automatic model fallbacks by SLA class (L1 -> L2 smaller model) and rate-based shedding for non-critical routes.
- Batching/windowing: keep batching windows < 20ms for interactive flows; longer windows for background/async to increase throughput.

A couple of quick heuristics:
- Treat avg tokens-per-response and avg tokens-per-request as your effective token load. For example, at 150 QPS * (60+120) tokens = 27,000 tokens/sec.
- If a single GPU (quantized) sustains ~60,000 tokens/sec at p95 latency for your model family, you need ~0.45 GPUs for steady-state (round up); add warm pool and 30% headroom, so ~1.25 -> 2 GPUs as a conservative start.

I'll let Laura drop a compact sizing calc with explicit numbers. Attached: proposed-admission-policy.yaml (stub) — this enforces per-route concurrency, token budgets, and a burst queue with drop policy.

Happy to hop on Wed 2/10 10am PT — calendly link below.

Sophie — adding a compact rightsizing calc and a few network notes. Kept it conservative for initial production.

Rightsizing (concrete example)
- Inputs (from your CSV): steady QPS = 150, peak short-burst = 1200 QPS, avg input tokens = 120, avg output tokens = 60.
- Effective token/sec at steady: 150 * (120 + 60) = 27,000 tokens/sec.
- Effective token/sec at peak: 1200 * (120 + 60) = 216,000 tokens/sec.

Assume model family benchmark: quantized-8 GPU = 70,000 tokens/sec (p95 latency target met), quantized-16 = 100,000 tokens/sec (lower latency but higher memory).

Steady-state GPU need (conservative): 27,000 / 70,000 = 0.39 -> round up to 1 GPU.
Peak transient absorb (fast spin-up + warm pool):
- Warm pool sizing: 20% of peak concurrency footprint. Peak tokens/sec 216,000 -> base GPUs = 216,000 / 70,000 = 3.09 -> round up to 4 GPUs.
- Warm pool = 20% of 4 ≈ 1 GPU (kept warm).
- Headroom buffer for unexpected bursts = +25% -> 4 * 1.25 = 5 GPUs target if you want to avoid any shedding during known campaigns.

Operational guidance:
- Admission policy: per-route concurrency cap = 6 concurrent requests per GPU (example), global TPS envelope = sum(token-budgets) across active routes. Use token budgets that map to your L1 SLA.
- KV cache: pin hot sessions to warm pool nodes to avoid cold-cache penalties; eviction: LRU with TTL 12h for session caches.
- Network: ensure 1.25x the expected egress bandwidth during peak to avoid TCQ buildup (for 216k tokens/sec at 8KB average payload, plan for ~2.5Gbps headroom).

I'll drop the detailed spreadsheet with the math to the Drive folder. Suggested agenda for the call: 1) review calc, 2) admission-policy walk-through, 3) staging rollout plan, 4) compliance checklist.

Laura Bennett
